findings.description: The 'data' bucket is explicitly intended to be public (per the inline comment), sets no ACL, has no bucket policy restricting access, and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block. Combined with the customer master object stored in it, this exposes sensitive customer data to anonymous readers.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects including customer-master.xlsx are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption.
No logging block is configured, so unauthorised access to this publicly exposed bucket leaves no audit trail for detection or forensics.
Versioning is not enabled, so objects can be silently overwritten or deleted with no recovery or tamper evidence — a real integrity risk given the bucket is public and force_destroy is set.
No bucket policy denying requests with aws:SecureTransport = false is attached, so objects in this public bucket can be retrieved over cleartext HTTP.

findings.issue_category: sensitive data in public unencrypted bucket
findings.description: A file named 'customer-master.xlsx', likely containing customer PII, is uploaded into the public, unencrypted 'data' bucket with no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument set on the object.
The financials bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving financial records stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured for a bucket holding financial data, so access is not auditable for detection or investigation.
Versioning is not enabled, so financial objects can be overwritten or deleted without recovery or tamper evidence, compounded by force_destroy = true.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a later ACL or policy change could expose financial data publicly with no guardrail.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is set on the operations bucket, so its objects are stored without enforced encryption.
The operations bucket has no logging block, leaving no record of access for audit or incident response.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, removing the defence-in-depth guardrail against accidental public exposure via a future ACL or policy change.
The data science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so potentially sensitive analytics datasets are stored unencrypted while the logs bucket uses SSE-KMS.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for this bucket, leaving no guardrail against future public ACLs or bucket policies.

The central log bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block and no object-lock/MFA-delete protection, while force_destroy = true permits the bucket and all audit evidence to be deleted; log data containing request metadata therefore has no guardrail against exposure or destruction.
